references.text: Abram builds an altar to the Lord after the Lord appeared to him. This pattern of building altars is repeated in Hebron.
Abram sets up an altar and calls on the name of the Lord, a practice he repeats at the oaks of Mamre in Hebron.
Abram returns to the altar at Bethel and calls on the name of the Lord—the same pattern of worship as when he built an altar in Hebron.
The Amorites of Mamre are mentioned as Abram’s ally, linking back to the oaks of Mamre in Hebron where Abram settled and built an altar.
The Lord appears to Abraham at the oaks of Mamre—the same place where Abram had settled and built an altar for the Lord.
Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah near Mamre (Hebron) as a burial site, showing the lasting significance of this place for the patriarch and his family.
Mamre (Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron) is mentioned as the place where Isaac lived, showing that the patriarchs’ connection to Hebron continued.
A clear thematic parallel demonstrating continuity in faith: both Abraham and Isaac build altars and call on the name of the Lord upon settling in a new place.
